At the same meeting Fred Ford won the 880 yards Open Handicap from the 80 yards mark; and Jack Williams was successful from 8¼ yards in the Open "100."

A team consisting of Tosh, Scrimshaw, Williams (J.S.), Powter, Gratte, Clemens, Kench, and Ford (A.J.) made up the club team. The start from Baker Street was not at all encouraging, as the rain was descending in torrents, accompanied by plenty of lightning and thunder.
Hampson ran the half-mile stage for us and handed over with a fair lead. This was increased by Purdy and retained by J.

Despite a very fine first leg by Jack Williams we were forced to take second place; but no mistake was made in the mile team race, in which we placed our four men in the first five, with Bill Rice the actual winner.

Pottinger won the boy's with a score of 23 pts out of a possible 24, and J.Williams won the youth's. Pottinger,incidentally, has done twenty feet in the long-jump - Not too bad for a lad just fifteen years old.
The youth's was won by J.Williams, who beat Dereck Wade by one point. (Dereck was last years boy's winner.) A.Mead was third, another who competed in each event, with a solid performance.

JACK WILLIAMS (220y). Aged 62, civil servant, took up Veteran Running after a 32 year rest.

Jack Williams, accompanied by his wife, came up from Brighton - he still competes in veteran sprint races. Syd King, a former Hon Treasurer and regular member of our walking training packs and teams; he too was accompanied by his wife, daughter of a former club stalwart the late Bill Redgrave.

With New Year's Day 1977 being on a Saturday we wonder what the programme will be. Amongst the spectators was Jack Williams and his wife who had travelled up from Brighton. Jack still keeps fit and indeed looks it.
Jack Williams, late of Belgrave and Veterans AC, departed from our ranks on August 6th. He joined Belgrave as a junior in the twenties and won several sprint titles.
Odd memories come back - Bill Merryman, Tommy Scrimshaw, Ernie Jarvis, my special pal Jack Williams (we still keep in touch with his widow Mavis), Bill Sutton and many others.
